decisive_items: intraepidermal and dermal perivascular neutrophilic infiltrate
response.rationale: R4 best matches the histopathologic pattern of leukocytoclastic vasculitis (neutrophilic perivascular infiltrate with vessel wall necrosis and fibrinoid necrosis) and the clinical ulcers/eschars. R3 is supported by positive ANA and anti-SSA/Ro but the histology and absence of systemic lupus features make it less specific. R1 has only low-titer P-ANCA, with no upper respiratory or renal evidence. R2 lacks MPO-ANCA or systemic medium-vessel features. R5 is overly broad. R6 lacks supporting lobular panniculitis or tuberculosis context.

rejected.why: P-ANCA is low (1:20); no granulomatous or upper airway/renal findings and MPO-ANCA is not characteristic of GPA.
No medium-vessel systemic involvement or classic Polyarteritis Nodosa biopsy features; focal fibrinoid necrosis alone is nonspecific.
ANA and anti-SSA/Ro are weak/non-specific and skin findings with leukocytoclastic vasculitis favor an isolated cutaneous vasculitis rather than lupus vasculitis.
Too broad; does not capture the specific neutrophilic vascular damage and clinical picture as precisely.
No lobular panniculitis or tuberculosis association; ulcer morphology alone is nonspecific.
